title: Quran, Sura 38 (ṣād) (Codex Parisino-petropolitanus)
source: Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (BnF Arabe 328) via Gallica IIIF + Corpus Coranicum folio mapping + Tanzil + Pickthall
description: Sura 38 (ṣād) from the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (c. 650-750 AD), one section per folio side, each linked to the exact Gallica image of that page (1 pages).
introduction:
Sura 38 (ṣād) as preserved on 1 folio side of the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (Paris, BnF Arabe 328 (a) and (b)), one of the oldest surviving Quran manuscripts, written in hijazi script on parchment, c. 650-750 AD. Each section below is one folio side, and the image shown is that exact page.

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side from Gallica (Bibliotheque nationale de France IIIF). The folio's sura:verse range was taken from the Corpus Coranicum "Manuscripta Coranica" record for that page, which states the first and last word on the page; the folio numbers of both services were cross-checked by comparing the two images pixel by pixel.
  2. Original text: the Arabic of the Tanzil Project Uthmani text (CC BY 3.0), reproduced unchanged, verse by verse.
  3. English: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain, verse by verse.

Orthography: the codex is written in scriptio defectiva: no vowel signs, almost no consonantal dots, long vowels often unwritten, and letter shapes that differ from the printed Uthmani text. The modern text given here therefore differs orthographically from what is on the folio while conveying the same reading; readers should expect, for example, the basmala and words such as qala to be spelled with fewer letters on the page.

Numbering: verse numbers follow the standard Kufan (Cairo 1924) division used by Corpus Coranicum, Tanzil and Pickthall. Early codices mark verse ends with ink dots that in places divide the text differently, so a verse count made on the page may not match these numbers exactly. In Tanzil's text the basmala opening each sura (except sura 9) is printed as part of verse 1. Where a page begins or ends in the middle of a verse the whole verse is given and the word position is stated in the section heading.

Lacunae: the surviving Paris leaves do not carry every verse of this sura. Only the verses listed in the sections below are on the folios shown; the rest of the sura is lost or preserved in other fragments of the same codex (St Petersburg Marcel 18, Vatican Ar. 1605/1, London KFQ 60) that are not included here.
translator_notes: 23 of 88 verses of this sura survive on the Paris leaves of the codex (1 folio side).
Corpus Coranicum records the first and last word of each page; a verse split across two pages is shown in full under both pages with the word position noted.

translation.original_ref: Quran 38:66-88, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 56r (page continues into sura 39 (39:4))
translation.original_text: <sup>66</sup>رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفَّٰرُ <sup>67</sup>قُلْ هُوَ نَبَؤٌا۟ عَظِيمٌ <sup>68</sup>أَنتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ <sup>69</sup>مَا كَانَ لِىَ مِنْ عِلْمٍۭ بِٱلْمَلَإِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰٓ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ <sup>70</sup>إِن يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ إِلَّآ أَنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ <sup>71</sup>إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى خَٰلِقٌۢ بَشَرًا مِّن طِينٍ <sup>72</sup>فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى فَقَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ <sup>73</sup>فَسَجَدَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ <sup>74</sup>إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ ٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ <sup>75</sup>قَالَ يَٰٓإِبْلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَىَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْعَالِينَ <sup>76</sup>قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍ <sup>77</sup>قَالَ فَٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ <sup>78</sup>وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ <sup>79</sup>قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ <sup>80</sup>قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ <sup>81</sup>إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْوَقْتِ ٱلْمَعْلُومِ <sup>82</sup>قَالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ <sup>83</sup>إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ <sup>84</sup>قَالَ فَٱلْحَقُّ وَٱلْحَقَّ أَقُولُ <sup>85</sup>لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ <sup>86</sup>قُلْ مَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ <sup>87</sup>إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ <sup>88</sup>وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُۥ بَعْدَ حِينٍۭ
translation.text: <sup>66</sup>Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the Mighty, the Pardoning. <sup>67</sup>Say: It is tremendous tidings <sup>68</sup>Whence ye turn away! <sup>69</sup>I had no knowledge of the Highest Chiefs when they disputed; <sup>70</sup>It is revealed unto me only that I may be a plain warner. <sup>71</sup>When thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to create a mortal out of mire, <sup>72</sup>And when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My Spirit, then fall down before him prostrate, <sup>73</sup>The angels fell down prostrate, every one, <sup>74</sup>Saving Iblis; he was scornful and became one of the disbelievers. <sup>75</sup>He said: O Iblis! What hindereth thee from falling prostrate before that which I have created with both My hands? Art thou too proud or art thou of the high exalted? <sup>76</sup>He said: I am better than him. Thou createdst me of fire, whilst him Thou didst create of clay. <sup>77</sup>He said: Go forth from hence, for lo! thou art outcast, <sup>78</sup>And lo! My curse is on thee till the Day of Judgment. <sup>79</sup>He said: My Lord! Reprieve me till the day when they are raised. <sup>80</sup>He said: Lo! thou art of those reprieved <sup>81</sup>Until the day of the time appointed. <sup>82</sup>He said: Then, by Thy might, I surely will beguile them every one, <sup>83</sup>Save Thy single-minded slaves among them. <sup>84</sup>He said: The Truth is, and the Truth I speak, <sup>85</sup>That I shall fill hell with thee and with such of them as follow thee, together. <sup>86</sup>Say (O Muhammad, unto mankind): I ask of you no fee for this, and I am no simulating. <sup>87</sup>Lo! it is naught else than a reminder for all peoples <sup>88</sup>And ye will come in time to know the truth thereof.
